messages:
maya: Heads up — cost dashboard is showing large negative cache savings for a handful of customers this morning. noticed after the 08:30 ingest. anyone else seeing weird negative totals?

sam: seeing a couple tenants with negative prefetched savings too. likely attribution leak. quick check: are we double-counting prefetch credits + hotpath KC cache hits?

leo: my hunch: sampling mismatch between the trace join and the token-metering table. if sample_rate != same-window we can under/over attribute.

erin: +1 on sampling. also the UI is currently summing raw credit deltas without clamping, so a noisy negative delta can flip the slab for the whole tenant. we should show a confidence band.

maya: sample numbers: tenant A had -$3.4k in cache_savings yesterday on the dashboard but billing preview shows +$1.2k. that's a big mismatch.

sam: can we get the raw query for that dashboard tile? I can run a replay.

leo: posting the dashboard query we use (simplified):
```sql
SELECT tenant_id, sum(prefetch_credit) as prefetch, sum(kv_hit_cost_saved) as kv_saved
FROM token_events_sampled
WHERE ts >= $start AND ts < $end AND sample_rate = 100
GROUP BY tenant_id;
```
Note: we assume sample_rate tag is present. if not, join uses default 1/100.

erin: and the meter table uses unsampled per-invocation counts. when we join sampled events to unsampled meter we upweight, but our weight function changed in last deploy (see PR #4123) — it used to use 1/sample_rate, now it uses a stochastic estimator that can go slightly negative under rare pathological inputs.

maya: ah that PR. ops-bot deployed that at 08:12?

ops-bot: deploy: rollout/estimator-v2 -> prod at 2026-03-21T08:12:14Z (sha: d4c9b2). Canary success: 3/3, 0 errors.

sam: ok probable cause. options: revert estimator PR, add clamp(max(0, weight)), or compute cache_saving as a separate join after reweighting. which do we want?

leo: short-term revert or clamp. long-term: rework join to use deterministic aggregation keys and store precomputed sample_weight per-window so UI queries are stable.

erin: UX asks: can we show a small warning on tiles when the underlying sample_rate < 100 or weight variance > threshold? they want explainability for PMs and CS.

maya: yes please. add a yellow caution badge: "est. variance high — sample-based estimate" and tooltip with link to docs + sample rate.

sam: I can ship a clamp and the badge. patch plan: revert not required. steps:
1) clamp weights to >=0 in estimator pipeline (fast)
2) add variance flag in the cost aggregation API (new field: sample_variance)
3) UI: show badge when sample_variance > 0.02 or sample_rate < 50
4) longer term: RFC to precompute stable weights per-billing-window

leo: watchouts: clamping will bias low — make sure we log before/after diffs to metrics (e.g., cost_api.bias.clamped_ratio). also check canary on a high-traffic tenant to confirm no perf regression.

erin: UX: for the tooltip copy: "Estimates are based on sampled telemetry. Small negative values may arise from estimator variance. See diagnostics." Want a link to an RFC page — @sam can you add test vectors?

sam: yes, I'll add unit tests + a small replay job to compare pre/post clamp on last 7 days. will post results to the thread.

maya: who owns the small UI badge? @erin?

erin: I can prototype the badge tomorrow. will add copy + link to the diag page once Sam posts results.

leo: also a related note: routing fallbacks create model-switch noise that makes per-model econ look worse. we should exclude transient fallback requests (retry -> fallback) from unit-econ tiles or show them as separate line series.

maya: good point. add to RFC: exclude requests with header `x-routing-fallback: true` from model-level breakdown by default. make it opt-in.

sam: API sketch for the aggregation endpoint (proposal):
POST /internal/econ/aggregate
body: {"start":"2026-03-14T00:00:00Z","end":"2026-03-21T00:00:00Z","group_by":["tenant_id","model_sku"],"filters":{"exclude_fallback":true}}
response: {"rows":[{"tenant_id":"t-123","model_sku":"gptx-1","unit_cost":123.45,"cache_savings":-12.34}], "sample_variance":0.034}

leo: +1 but use GET for small queries and POST for large ones. also consider pagination for long windows.

maya: timeline: Sam to push pipeline clamp + replay by EOD. Erin prototype badge by EOW. Leo to draft RFC for stable weight precompute (next sprint). Maya to coordinate with CS for tenant A billing recon.

sam: starting replay job now. will paste diff when done.

ops-bot: job:replay-weights-2026-03-21 started (job id: replay-8812).

leo: thanks everyone. small follow-up: add a simple dashboard test asserting billing_preview ~ display_total within 5% for top-20 tenants to catch this earlier.

maya: agreed. creating GH issue and will add notification to the cost-monitoring alert.

sam: replay done — clamping reduces negative deltas significantly for tenant A. diff summary: tenant_A_display:-3400 -> +980 (billing preview +1.2k unchanged). uploading logs to /tmp/replay-8812-summary.log

erin: great, I'll wire the badge to show variance=0.034 for tenant A until RFC.

maya: ok moving to action items. thanks team :thumbsup:
